# Invariants

Every named rule `paceq fsck` checks, what a finding means, and what to do
about it. The catalogue lives in internal/store/invariants.go beside the
sweep itself; this page is generated from it, so a check that changes here
changes there too.

## Severity

| Grade | Meaning | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| critical | a uniqueness rule or the dependency graph is broken: a hand edit or corruption, not a bug paceq can reason around | the daemon refuses to start; `paceq fsck --repair --confirm` repairs what is repairable, after the operator confirms |
| serious | state drift the system can reconcile out of: a dead lease, a step outliving its run | an event is recorded and monitoring sees it; the daemon keeps serving |
| warning | cosmetic or historic: rows an older paceq wrote differently | reported and logged; nothing refuses |

## The catalogue

### I1 — a run in running holds a live lease

Severity: **serious**.

the reaper clears this on its own within one lease TTL; paceq fsck --repair requeues the run now with epoch+1 and reason RUN_ORPHANED_RECONCILED

### I10 — a run's stored state is what its steps aggregate to

Severity: **serious**.

paceq explain run <id> shows both stories; the reconciler repairs the aggregate on its next sweep

### I11 — the fencing token never falls

Severity: **serious**.

an unfenced write happened; report it as a bug with the events of the named run (paceq export run <id>)

### I12 — no job or concurrency key runs past its ceiling

Severity: **serious**.

admission control and the claim both enforce this on the way in; report it as a bug with the job name

### I13 — timestamps are monotone: created <= started <= finished, and a present stamp is a real one

Severity: **warning**.

a clock jump under way; check the machine's clock sync with paceq doctor

### I14 — a run held for the future carries its defer reason

Severity: **warning**.

paceq fsck --repair stamps the reason as unspecified, which the CLI then reports as held for an unknown reason

### I15 — every event's from_state is the event before it, per run and per step

Severity: **warning**.

a hole in the history makes explain incomplete; report it as a bug with paceq export run <id>

### I2 — a terminal run has no step still pending or running

Severity: **serious**.

paceq fsck --repair cancels the stranded steps with a reason code, exactly as a shutdown would

### I3 — one run per (job, run_key)

Severity: **critical**.

the unique rule is enforced by the schema, so a break means a hand edit or corruption; keep a copy of the state directory and restore from backup

### I5 — a step's attempt counter sits inside its budget

Severity: **serious**.

a row was written behind the transition layer; report it as a bug with paceq export run <id>

### I6 — at most one tick per (source_kind, source_name, scheduled_for)

Severity: **critical**.

the unique rule is enforced by the schema, so a break means a hand edit or corruption; keep a copy of the state directory and restore from backup

### I8 — a running step has every step it needs succeeded

Severity: **serious**.

the claim predicate gates on the same rule, so this is drift; report it as a bug with paceq export run <id>

### I9 — the step dependency graph is acyclic and names existing steps

Severity: **critical**.

a cyclic run can never finish: cancel it with paceq cancel run <id> and fix the job spec; a dangling edge means the job spec was edited mid-run

### reason — a terminal row carries a usable reason code

Severity: **warning**.

rows from an older paceq; paceq fsck --repair stamps them as legacy, new rows are refused by the schema
